newsitem.title: USA: MGE wheat closes lower on bearish export sentiment.
newsitem.headline: MGE wheat closes lower on bearish export sentiment.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed lower on bearish input from the export sector including talk that India cancelled a tender for 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat, traders said.
"There was just a lack of demand," a trader said. "That showed up in the drop in the spot month."
The nearby May contract closed 5-3/4 cents per bushel lower at $4.12-1/2.
New crop September closed lower but gained two cents per bushel in its spread with May. September found underpinning from Monday's USDA March planting intentions report.
USDA early Monday said U.S. farmers would plant 17.775 million acres of spring wheat this year, below an average of analysts' estimates for 18.55 million.
The government Monday said U.S. wheat stocks as of March 1 totaled 822 million bushels, below analysts' average estimate of 827 million bushels.
MGE new crop September spring wheat futures closed 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower at $4.03-1/4.
